claims.supporting_quote: Phosphorus and potassium values are P2O5 and K2O. The CDH-derived full-cycle matrix totals about 1200 kg/ha of 10-10-20 for tomato, corresponding to 120 kg N, 120 kg P2O5 and 240 kg K2O per hectare, and this is used as the central market-gardening recommendation. citeturn30search11 A Senegal tomato seed-production protocol gives a more compositionally targeted sandy-soil program with a calculated balance of roughly 112-130 N, 146 P2O5 and 204 K2O kg/ha, and notes a general seed-crop recommendation near 100-150-200 N-P2O5-K2O; this independently places the central values in a realistic Senegalese intensive-production range. citeturn30search6turn31search10 Older CDH-derived documentation describes tomato as preferring soils that are not too heavy, but deep, loose and organic-matter-rich. citeturn30search12 FAO EcoCrop similarly lists medium/organic texture as optimal and well-drained conditions as preferred. citeturn23search0 Min and max NPK values are a minus/plus 20% engineering envelope around the CDH central prescription because no official ISRA/CDH three-point nutrient threshold was located; they should not be interpreted as physiological toxicity limits. claims.supporting_quote: For the fertilizer fields, phosphorus is expressed as P2O5 and potassium as K2O, matching the Senegalese 10-10-20 fertilizer convention. A CDH-derived Senegal matrix gives about 1000 kg/ha of 10-10-20 over the onion crop cycle, equivalent to 100 kg N, 100 kg P2O5 and 200 kg K2O per hectare; this is used as the central recommendation. citeturn30search11 Older Senegal/CDH onion practice also documents repeated 10-10-20 dressings, while a Senegal seed-production protocol uses a substantially more intensive, soil- and objective-specific program, confirming that fertilizer rates should ultimately be adjusted to soil analysis rather than interpreted as physiological constants. citeturn30search3turn30search4 Because the CDH sheets generally publish a central prescription rather than formal min/optimal/max thresholds, min and max here are a transparent engineering screening envelope of minus/plus 20% around the local CDH central dose; they are not published physiological deficiency or toxicity limits. Onion is treated as a light-to-medium, well-drained-soil crop: FAO EcoCrop identifies medium/organic texture as optimal while allowing a broad textural range, consistent with production on Senegal's sandy Niayes and lighter River Valley soils. citeturn23search3 The clay/sand percentages are therefore conservative numerical screening envelopes derived from USDA texture classes rather than literal ISRA granulometric thresholds; USDA NRCS classifies texture from measured sand, silt and clay fractions. citeturn28search0 The local Dior/Deck-Dior mapping was cross-checked against the supplied Senegal baseline, in which Dior is extremely sandy and Deck/Deck-Dior contains more fines. fileciteturn0file0 CEC is likewise an engineering soil-quality filter, because no crop-specific onion CEC cutoff was found in ISRA/CDH sheets: productive Niayes soils have reported CEC values around 8-34 cmol(+)/kg, whereas sandy soils commonly have much lower nutrient-retention capacity. citeturn28search6turn29search3turn29search16

claims.supporting_quote: Phosphorus and potassium are P2O5 and K2O. The CDH-derived Senegal matrix specifies 500 kg/ha 10-10-20 at establishment and 300 kg/ha at each of two maintenance stages, totaling 1100 kg/ha 10-10-20 or 110 N, 110 P2O5 and 220 K2O kg/ha per crop cycle. citeturn30search14turn30search11 The min and max are a minus/plus 20% engineering band around that central CDH application, because a formal ISRA/CDH three-point nutrient-response threshold was not found. For texture, carrot is deliberately assigned the sandiest screening window after watermelon: root quality is favored by loose soils, and Senegal horticultural analysis reports carrot/navet production concentrated on the white-dune environments of the Niayes. citeturn20view2 FAO EcoCrop lists medium/organic soil as optimal but allows light soils within its absolute range; it also requires a well-drained root zone. citeturn27view0 The USDA Loamy Sand-Sandy Loam translation therefore gives a conservative 3-18% clay and 55-90% sand engine window. Because sandy carrot soils can have intrinsically low exchange capacity, the CEC minimum is set at 3 cmol(+)/kg rather than the higher values used for leafy vegetables, while 5-12 cmol(+)/kg is preferred; low-CEC fields require more frequent split fertilization, organic amendment and tighter irrigation management. FAO notes that low CEC indicates weak nutrient retention, and sandy-loam CEC commonly lies in the low single digits to around 10. citeturn29search3turn29search16
